1 Order on Writ Petition Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Utkarsh Birla learned Advocate appearing for respondent no. 4 and learned Standing Counsel for the State respondents.
The challenge in the present writ petition is to the notifications dated 27.8.2009 and 9.4.2010 of acquisition of land comprising of Gata No. 967 area 0.4680 hectares in revenue Village Sadarpur,
Pargana Dasna, Tehsil and District Ghaziabad, on the ground that the proceedings of acquisition stood lapsed in view of Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

sentences.text:
Another prayer in the writ petition is to quash the award dated 30.12.2013 and to declare a fresh award under Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (In short as "the Act, 2013").
Considering the said prayer made in the writ petition

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: , we raised a pointed query to the learned counsel for the petitioners to explain the latches in filing the present writ petition after a period of approximately nine years.
No explanation has been placed before us.

The contention in the present writ petition is that the petitioner had not accepted the award passed by the competent authority and kept on approaching the competent authority for declaration of fresh award under Section 24 of the Act, 2013.
This explanation does not stand to reason to sustain the challenge to the acquisition notifications issued in the year 2009-10, treating them as having been lapsed.

We may further record that the award dated 30.12.2013 appended with the writ petition records that none of the tenure holders come forward to submit their objections in reply to the notice dated 31.5.2019 issued under Section 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
This assertion in the award impugned is not objected in the writ petition.
Keeping in view of the above facts, we find that the acquisition proceedings stood concluded with the declaration of the award on 30.12.2013.
The challenge to the said proceedings cannot be sustained after a period of more than nine years without any justifiable explanation on the part of the petitioners.
The writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
